events.title: Macbeth Kills King Duncan I
events.description: Macbeth killed Duncan I of Scotland in battle and had himself crowned king. His reign lasted about 17 years. Shakespeare later turned the story into one of his best-known tragedies, though the real history differs a great deal from the play.
events.significance: The event started Macbeth's long rule over Scotland. It also became the historical basis for one of the most famous plays in English literature.

events.title: Columbus Reaches the Central American Mainland
events.description: On his fourth and final voyage, Christopher Columbus landed on the coast of present-day Honduras. It was the first time he set foot on the mainland of the Americas, after years of exploring Caribbean islands.
events.significance: The landing brought Spanish explorers to the Central American coast. Spain later colonized the region.

events.title: Roosevelt Signs the Social Security Act
events.description: President Franklin D. Roosevelt signed the Social Security Act into law during the Great Depression. The law created a national system of old-age benefits and unemployment insurance for American workers.
events.significance: It became the foundation of the American social safety net. It still supports tens of millions of retirees and families.

events.title: Pakistan Becomes an Independent Nation
events.description: As British rule in South Asia ended, Pakistan became a sovereign state. It consisted of West Pakistan, which is today's Pakistan, and East Pakistan, which is today's Bangladesh. India became independent the next day.
events.significance: The Partition of India reshaped South Asia. It displaced millions of people and created borders and rivalries that still matter today.
